I also checked uses of `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis`; the only one outside this file is `trace_baseChange` in LinearAlgebra/Trace.lean. The `Basis.baseChange` definition is the same in the setting of this file's `basis`: both take an R-basis of M and an R-algebra A that is only a `Semiring`, and both give an A-basis of A ⊗[R] M indexed by ι. Their repr formulas differ in form: `baseChange_repr_tmul` gives `b.repr y i • x` and `basis_repr_tmul` gives `a • mapRange (algebraMap R A) ..`, but they are propositionally equal. I could not compile anything. I did not confirm that every import is available transitively, or that the instance `Module.Free A A` and the `IsScalarTower R A A` instance resolve inside the `Module.Free.tensor` migration. They very likely do. The other declarations in the file are lemmas, instances or specialisations, not independent concepts. I did not flag the `toMatrix_baseChange`/`baseChange_linearMap` statements, because the rubric excludes duplicate theorem statements.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def basis : Basis ι A (A ⊗[R] M) where
  repr := { basisAux A b with map_smul' := basisAux_map_smul b }
findings.problem: Mathlib already has `Module.Basis.baseChange`. It has the same type: for `b : Basis ι R M` and `[Semiring S] [Algebra R S]`, it gives `Basis ι S (S ⊗[R] M)`. It satisfies `baseChange_apply : b.baseChange S i = 1 ⊗ₜ b i` and `baseChange_repr_tmul`. It is built from the more general `Basis.tensorProduct`, which already comes with its own API and `Module.Free.tensor`. This file builds a second, separate A-basis of `A ⊗[R] M`, using a hand-rolled `basisAux` and an `ext`/`simp` proof of A-linearity (`basisAux_map_smul`). It also re-proves the same simp API: `basis_apply` is `baseChange_apply`, and `basis_repr_tmul` is `baseChange_repr_tmul` up to rewriting. So the library has two non-defeq presentations of the same basis. Its only outside user, `trace_baseChange` in LinearAlgebra/Trace.lean, uses `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis`, while the Kaehler and Cotangent files use `Basis.baseChange`. Simp lemmas for one do not fire on the other.
findings.proposed_change: Make `Module.Basis.baseChange` the single definition. Redefine `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis A b` as `b.baseChange A` (or deprecate it), and delete `basisAux`, `basisAux_tmul` and `basisAux_map_smul`. Keep `basis_repr_tmul` and `basis_repr_symm_apply'` only if needed, as thin corollaries of `Basis.baseChange_repr_tmul` and `Basis.baseChange_apply`. Restate `Basis.baseChange_linearMap`, `Basis.baseChange_end` and `toMatrix_baseChange` for `b.baseChange A`. Switch `trace_baseChange` to `b.baseChange A`. The hypotheses match (`CommSemiring R`, `Semiring A`, `Algebra R A`), so no assumptions are lost. Since `basis_apply` is already `1 ⊗ₜ b i`, the proofs of `baseChange_linearMap` should go through with `Basis.baseChange_apply`. Only the `basis_repr_symm_apply'` proof needs a small reproof.
findings.benefit: The library gets one canonical base-change basis. Simp lemmas and results such as `Basis.baseChange_apply` and `liftBaseChange_injective_iff` then apply to the bases used in the matrix and trace lemmas. About 25 lines of bespoke construction are removed, and `Module.Free.tensor` and the `Basis.tensorProduct` API are reused.

def baseChange (b : Basis ι R M) : Basis ι S (S ⊗[R] M) :=
  (tensorProduct (.singleton Unit S) b).reindex (Equiv.punitProd ι)
(b.baseChange S).repr (x ⊗ₜ y) i = b.repr y i • x

findings.problem: This is a second route to freeness of `A ⊗[R] M`, via the duplicate basis. Mathlib already has the general instance `Module.Free.tensor [Module.Free S M] [Module.Free R N] : Module.Free S (M ⊗[R] N)`. Taking `S := A`, `M := A` and `N := M` gives the same statement here, since `Module.Free A A` is an instance. Its proof uses `Basis.tensorProduct`, not this file's `basis`.
findings.proposed_change: Once `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis` is replaced by `Basis.baseChange`, prove this instance as `Module.Free.of_basis ((Module.Free.chooseBasis R M).baseChange A)`. Alternatively, check whether `Module.Free.tensor` already provides it and delete this instance. In that case, check that the instance diamond-free resolution still works for downstream `Module.Free A (A ⊗[R] M)` uses.
findings.benefit: This removes a parallel instance path to the same fact and ties the file's headline result to the shared tensor-product basis API.
